11.t: Working with data: mass and weight
q: What was the weight of the 0.3 kg mass?
Use W = m × 10 to calculate the expected weight of 0.4 kg.
Describe the relationship shown by the graph.
Weight is proportional to mass: a straight line through the origin; doubling the mass doubles the weight.
Use the graph to estimate the mass of a stone that weighs 2.5 N, and suggest why her readings are a little below mass × 10.
About 0.25 kg. On Earth gravity is about 9.8 N per kg, not exactly 10; also reading errors and the newton meter’s accuracy.
